title: task view has no field/note projection; returns all implementationNotes unbounded
description:
Raised by opum-agent (2026-09-13, durable copy OPAG-120) from a live proof-graph inspection: a research task on that probe already exceeds a million characters of implementationNotes, so a plain task view means loading a history nobody asked for. quest help task view advertises no projection or note-selection flags today -- a caller always gets the full record.

Proposed shape (opum-agent's framing, not settled here): select which top-level fields come back; fetch only the latest notes, or notes since a stable cursor; retrieve one complete note by a stable id/digest when the full text is actually needed (e.g. for proof evidence); and an explicit hard output budget whose response carries omitted-record/field metadata so a caller can tell truncation from completeness. The constraint opum-agent flagged as worth keeping: a bounded view must not become the ONLY way to read a note -- an exact, unbounded read needs to stay available.

Companion finding on the Lore side already sent to lore-cli (its context can retain a target larger than maxTokens while marking the result truncated) -- neither half fixes the other; this task is Quest's half only.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task view supports selecting a subset of top-level fields in its output
quest task view supports retrieving only the latest N implementationNotes, or notes since a given cursor, without fetching the full array
a single implementationNote can be retrieved in full by a stable id/digest independent of any bounded/paginated view
a bounded/paginated task view response carries metadata indicating what was omitted (which fields, how many notes), so truncation is distinguishable from completeness
an unbounded exact-read path remains available and documented for evidence use, not removed in favor of the bounded default

plan: Per DEC-3 (agreed cross-repo 2026-09-14): add opt-in --max-notes N to task view only, out of the 5 original ACs -- --fields, --since/cursor, single-note-by-digest are explicitly deferred by DEC-3, not implemented here.
CLI: parse --max-notes as a positive integer in main.ts view handler (generalize limitValue into a shared positive-integer helper), pass through TaskCommandRequest.

Keep application/tasks/tasks.ts view()/viewWithPath() returning the full untrimmed record (source of truth); do the implementationNotes capping + notesOmitted projection at the CLI boundary in dispatchTrackerTaskCommand (src/cli/commands/task/index.ts), slicing the array tail since notes append chronologically (mergeList pushes new entries at the end).
notesOmitted is present (even at 0) only when --max-notes was supplied; absent entirely on the unchanged default path.

Update command-contract.ts manifest (filters: ["max-notes"], fields += notesOmitted) and sweep every mirrored assertion: test/contract/command-contract.test.ts golden, src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts + index.ts probe() required table (both exact-match tested), command-help.ts task view entry, and test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts QCLI-137 field-presence test which needs to account for notesOmitted being conditionally present.
Run bun run check to green; manually exercise --max-notes against a multi-note task as AC evidence.

Check off only the ACs the DEC-3-scoped implementation actually satisfies; leave the rest unchecked with a note explaining the DEC-3 narrowing, and report the AC/DEC-3 scope mismatch back rather than resolve it unilaterally.
implementationNotes:
Implemented the DEC-3-scoped shape only: quest task view <id> [--max-notes N]. Absent --max-notes, output is byte-for-byte unchanged (verified manually: no notesOmitted key present). With --max-notes N, implementationNotes is capped to the tail N entries (notes append chronologically -- mergeList in application/tasks/edit-patch.ts pushes new entries at the array end, so most-recent-N is the tail slice) and a notesOmitted sibling field is always present, including 0 when nothing was capped. Verified live against a 5-note task: --max-notes 2 -> [note 4, note 5], notesOmitted:3; --max-notes 999 -> all 5 notes, notesOmitted:0; --max-notes 0 and --max-notes abc both fail usage (exit 2) via a shared positiveIntegerValue helper generalized out of --limit.

Capping happens at the CLI boundary (dispatchTrackerTaskCommand in src/cli/commands/task/index.ts), not in application/tasks/tasks.ts -- view()/viewWithPath() keep returning the full untrimmed record as the source of truth for any other caller, matching how task list --limit is structured.

Swept every mirrored assertion of the task view manifest entry beyond the two named in the brief: src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts (trackerManifestFixture) and the inline required table inside QuestTrackerClient.probe() in src/contract/tracker/index.ts both do an EXACT sorted-array comparison against the live manifest (exercised by test/contract/tracker/quest-tracker-client.test.ts), so both needed the same filters/fields additions or probe() would have thrown a drift error. Also had to adjust test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts (QCLI-137, "every task field the manifest declares is a field the CLI emits"): notesOmitted is deliberately the one task-view field that is NOT always emitted (absent by design when --max-notes is not supplied per DEC-3), so that generalized field-presence test needed an explicit carve-out plus a direct present/absent assertion pair, or it would fail by design once notesOmitted joined the manifest fields list.

bun run check: 483 pass, 0 fail, across 56 files (typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check, full test suite) -- fully green.

AC/DEC-3 scope mismatch, reported rather than resolved unilaterally: this task record still carries opum-agents original 5-item framing (filed 2026-09-13, before DEC-3 was agreed 2026-09-14). DEC-3 explicitly narrows quest-side scope to --max-notes only and explicitly defers --fields (AC 1/position 1), --since/cursor-based selection (half of AC 2/position 2), per-note-by-digest retrieval (AC 3/position 3), and field-level omission metadata (half of AC 4/position 4) as later work with no concrete pain point yet. Only AC 5/position 5 (unbounded default stays available and documented) is checked, with direct evidence. The other four stay unchecked -- not because the work failed, but because DEC-3 is the authoritative narrowing and I did not want to check an AC on the strength of a decision record rather than a delivered capability. Did not run quest task complete for the same reason: this PR does not deliver the tasks last criterion as originally written. Left status at In Progress. Did not file follow-up tasks for the deferred items per the standing QCLI-279/QCLI-290 id-allocation constraint on quest task create -- reporting this back instead.
finalSummary:
Delivered the DEC-3-scoped shape: quest task view <id> --max-notes N, additive/opt-in, unchanged default. Caps implementationNotes to the tail N entries and adds notesOmitted (present, including 0, whenever --max-notes is supplied; absent otherwise) -- verified live against a 5-note task. Merged via PR #84.

The other four acceptance criteria (field selection via --fields, --since/cursor note selection, per-note-by-digest retrieval, field-level omission metadata) are this task's ORIGINAL framing from 2026-09-13, filed before DEC-3 (2026-09-14, quest decision view DEC-3) deliberately narrowed quest's side of the shared quest/lore-cli shape to --max-notes only -- DEC-3's own text: "may follow later if a concrete pain point appears; none exists today the way it does for notes." They stay unchecked because DEC-3 is the authoritative narrowing, not because the work failed or was skipped. Completing anyway per DEC-1's advisory-acceptance-criteria convention, which exists for exactly this: an honestly unchecked item reported via unresolvedAtCompletion rather than silently dropped.
